doc.title: DataSentinel — Noa Tournoy
doc.desc: DataSentinel: a dashboard for monitoring the security of digital products, built during a three-month internship at ADEO. Looker, LookML, Python, React, BigQuery, Terraform, Kubernetes.
c.b: June → August 2025, internship at ADEO Ronchin
c.c: Looker · LookML · Python · React · BigQuery · Terraform
lede: A dashboard that replaced the manual tracking of digital-product security, and the full-stack extensions that make it usable day to day.
sujet.t: From spreadsheets to a single source.
sujet.1: Security tracking for digital products lived in hand-maintained spreadsheets: vulnerability status, compliance, penetration-test progress. Every cross-check was copy work, and nobody held the same version of the number.
sujet.2: DataSentinel centralises that monitoring in a Looker dashboard wired straight to the data. The number on screen is the number at the source; there is no intermediate version left to maintain.
f1.p: Working the data through Google Cloud Platform and BigQuery: complex SQL queries and modelling in LookML. This is the layer that decides what an indicator means: the place where a vague definition costs the most.
f2.p: A dashboard shows; it does not let you act. I built extensions embedded in Looker (Python backend, React frontend) to make penetration-test management interactive: consult, update and follow up inside the tool rather than beside it.
f3.p: A continuous integration and delivery pipeline, and infrastructure described as code: Terraform, GitHub Actions, Docker, Kubernetes. The tool redeploys without a manual step.
f4.p: The Google Looker and LookML certifications, and one conviction: on a security subject, the value is not in the chart but in the definition of the data it displays.
confid.p: No screenshots, no data, no product names: the contents of the tool belong to ADEO. What is described here is limited to what I can say about my own work.
